script.base: Market says IND leads: implied totals IND 26.8 / LV 19.8 in a closed roof, moderate 46.5. Base flow is D. Jones and Jonathan Taylor (59 car / 343 yds, weeks 2-4) getting IND in front by a score, then Taylor closing the clock, while G. Smith (11 car / 56 rush yds in that window) has to throw to Jakobi Meyers (23 tgt), Brock Bowers (19 tgt, knee questionable) and Tre Tucker (19 tgt) to stay in range. Not a 14-point blowout lock and not a shootout.
script.flip1: IND is up 14+ early, Taylor's carries spike, IND pass volume (Pittman, Warren, Downs) stalls after halftime, and LV catchers only eat in garbage time while Jeanty's rush share dies.
script.flip2: LV hangs or leads into the IND coverage absences (Kenny Moore II and Daniel Scott out), IND cannot sit on Taylor, D. Jones throws more, and Jeanty keeps a full carry day. That flip kills a Taylor rush over and boosts IND and LV pass volume.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost because LV never let IND lead. Moore and Scott being out showed up in Meyers (23 recent targets) and Tucker, the game stayed one score or flipped, and Taylor finished in the 71-76 band while a 4.18 YPC front stacked him — the 165-yard game was the fluke the median was hiding. Downs repeated his 24-yard week because Mitchell, not the slot, took Pierce's 10 targets and 181 air yards, and the second-half clock ended his routes before 29.5. A Bowers inactive would not have saved these two IND legs; they needed IND to play from in front and the Pierce vacuum to hit Downs, and neither had to happen.
slip_story: One story only: controlled IND lead, about a 27-20 type game, not a shootout and not a 17-point blowout. Taylor rush over is the clock leg; Downs rec over is the underneath leg that still works while IND scores toward 26.8. They win together if the lead stays inside two scores. Do not add a total under, a Jeanty rush over, or an LV pass over — those need flip 2. Two legs, no TDs, one market per player.
